    Square-zero lifts of modules and maps (Lemma 6.6) #

    positive-deformations.tex (lem:square-zero-selected-lifts): for a Hochschild two-cocycle μ of internal degree q > 0 of a graded algebra Λ over R (a field or ℤ/4), put Λ_μ = (Λ ⊗ R[ε]/(ε²), m + εμ). "Write a lifted action as ma + εν_i(m,a). Its equation is ν_i(ma,b) − ν_i(m,ab) + ν_i(m,a)b = mμ(a,b). […] The degree-q Ext² vanishing supplies ν_i. […] The difference of two solutions is a bar one-cocycle of degree q; the Ext¹ vanishing makes it the coboundary of a degree-q coordinate change. […] For a degree-r map f, write its lift as f + εg. Its equation is g(ma) − g(m)a = ν_j(f(m),a) − f(ν_i(m,a)). […] Since r ≥ 0, the Ext¹ vanishing supplies g. […] Let F_1, …, F_h lift a basis f_1, …, f_h of an original Hom module […] This proves freeness."

    Formalization: the lifted module and maps are recorded by their first-order equations (ActLift, IsLiftHom), with R[ε]-linear structure ε·(f, g) = (0, f); the regular lift at a cyclic projective is ν = μ (CycProj.actLift, the paper's "If M_i = e_xΛ, the regular module e_xΛ_μ is such a lift"). The additional gradings of the lemma are in SquareZeroWeight.lean.

                          Freeness of lifted Hom modules: lifts (f_l, g_l) of a basis f_l of the original Hom module form an R[ε]-basis, i.e. every lifted map is uniquely Σ c_l (f_l, g_l) + Σ c'_l ε(f_l, g_l) with ε(f, g) = (0, f).

                          Trivializing derivations #

                          The algebra step of the injectivity in Proposition 7.6 (weights-and-parameters.tex): a lift of the left multiplications to the lifted regular module, written through its value Δ on the regular module and split by a complete family of idempotents, makes μ a coboundary.
